module_title: Advanced Networking - Device Mapping, PDUs, and Gateways
introduction: Tailored for SSC CGL Tier-2 (Mains) and technical IT Officer exams, this advanced module maps physical devices to their exact OSI layers, defines Protocol Data Units (PDUs), and explains protocol conversion via Gateways.

core_concepts.title: Protocol Data Units (PDUs)
core_concepts.description:
As data moves through the OSI layers, its format and name change:
- Physical Layer: Data is raw 0s and 1s, called 'Bits'.
- Data Link Layer: Data is packaged into 'Frames'.
- Network Layer: Data is packaged into 'Packets'.
- Transport Layer: Data is divided into 'Segments'.

core_concepts.title: Device to Layer Mapping
core_concepts.description:
Examiners will ask which device operates at which layer:
- Hub & Repeater: Operate at the Physical Layer (Layer 1).
- Switch & Bridge: Operate at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2) using MAC Addresses.
- Router: Operates at the Network Layer (Layer 3) using IP Addresses.

core_concepts.title: Gateway (The Protocol Converter)
core_concepts.description: The most advanced networking device. It is used to connect two networks that run on 'Completely Different Protocols' or architectures (e.g., connecting a Windows network to an Apple network mainframe). It acts as a universal translator.

core_concepts.title: Critical Layer Functions
core_concepts.description:
- Network Layer: Responsible for 'Routing' and 'Logical Addressing' (IP).
- Transport Layer: Known as the 'Heart' of the OSI. Responsible for end-to-end error-free delivery using TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) and UDP.

important_entities.name: Repeater
important_entities.significance: When data travels over long cables, the signal gets weak (attenuation). A Repeater catches the weak signal, amplifies/regenerates it to its original strength, and sends it further down the line. It operates blindly at Layer 1.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In Tier-2, you must know that MAC Addresses strictly function at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2). IP Addresses strictly function at the Network Layer (Layer 3). Do not mix them up.
If an exam asks 'In what format does a Router transmit data?', the answer is 'Packets'. Because a Router sits at Layer 3, and the PDU for Layer 3 is a Packet.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Layer 1 = Hub, Layer 2 = Switch, Layer 3 = Router
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Memorizing this simple 1-2-3 hardware ladder will solve 90% of device-mapping questions in networking.

exam_strategy_tips: In Mains papers, the distinction between a Router and a Gateway is critical. If the question explicitly mentions connecting networks with 'Different Protocols' or 'Dissimilar Architectures', the answer is unequivocally Gateway.
